3The order is cancelled because an item is out of stockRight outcome: Cancelled, with Description naming the products without stock
4Payment is taken for the orderRight outcome: Paid, with the order total taken once from the buyer's payment method
5The order is cancelled because payment failedRight outcome: Cancelled, with no payment taken
6The order is cancelled at the customer's requestRight outcome: Cancelled before any payment is taken

MeasureCounted fromWhat exists, and what it needs
Data stored, not yet counted (3)
1Orders placedorders table, ordering database, order dateNeeds: a query on that table, collected by monitoring; no change to the application. Exists: the data, in orders table, ordering database, order date.
2Orders still openorders table, ordering database, orders not cancelled, by order dateNeeds: a query on that table, collected by monitoring; no change to the application. Exists: the data, in orders table, ordering database, orders not cancelled, by order date.
3Orders cancelled, by reasonorders table, ordering database, cancelled orders by their descriptionNeeds: a query on that table, collected by monitoring; no change to the application. Exists: the data, in orders table, ordering database, cancelled orders by their description.
Comes from outside the application (1)
1Orders deliverednot in the code: a delivery record per order; nothing is written after an order shipsNeeds: that organisation's records, if they can be had. Would count: not countable: the application records nothing after Shipped.
Instrumented: the application produces the measure and sends it to monitoring. The whole flow: 0 of 4 measures sent to monitoring. Read from the code and its monitoring set-up, not from a running system.
MeasureCounted fromWhat exists, and what it needs
Not produced: the application has to be changed (1)
1Mobile app order and cancel calls that failnot in the code: the mobile app reporting its failed order and cancel callsNeeds: the developers to add it to the application. Would count: failed calls seen by the app.
Data stored, not yet counted (3)
1Orders placed with a line at other than the catalogue priceorder lines table, ordering database, against catalog items table and event log table, catalog databaseNeeds: a query on that table, collected by monitoring; no change to the application. Exists: the data, in order lines table, ordering database, against catalog items table and event log table, catalog database.
2Ordering outbox rows not published, by Stateevent log table, ordering database, rows not yet published or failedNeeds: a query on that table, collected by monitoring; no change to the application. Exists: the data, in event log table, ordering database, rows not yet published or failed.
3Catalog outbox rows by Stateevent log table, catalog database, rows by publish stateNeeds: a query on that table, collected by monitoring; no change to the application. Exists: the data, in event log table, catalog database, rows by publish state.
Produced, but nothing collects it (12)
1Queue Ordering: messages waiting and consumersmessage broker's queue status (RabbitMQ), Ordering queueNeeds: monitoring to collect it; no change to the application. Exists: rabbitmqctl list_queues name messages consumers, row Ordering.
2Queue Catalog: messages waiting and consumersmessage broker's queue status (RabbitMQ), Catalog queueNeeds: monitoring to collect it; no change to the application. Exists: rabbitmqctl list_queues name messages consumers, row Catalog.
3Connections to the postgres server against max_connectionsdatabase server's own status (PostgreSQL), connections against its connection limitNeeds: monitoring to collect it; no change to the application. Exists: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity.
4Ordering database accepting connectionsdatabase server's own status (PostgreSQL), ordering database accepting connectionsNeeds: monitoring to collect it; no change to the application. Exists: pg_isready -d orderingdb.
5Long-running statements on orderingdbdatabase server's own status (PostgreSQL), statements on the ordering database running over five secondsNeeds: monitoring to collect it; no change to the application. Exists: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname = 'orderingdb' AND state = 'active' AND now() - ….
6Catalog database accepting connectionsdatabase server's own status (PostgreSQL), catalog database accepting connectionsNeeds: monitoring to collect it; no change to the application. Exists: pg_isready -d catalogdb.
7Long-running statements on catalogdbdatabase server's own status (PostgreSQL), statements on the catalog database running over five secondsNeeds: monitoring to collect it; no change to the application. Exists: the same count as the measure above, with datname = 'catalogdb'.
8Connections to the postgres server from catalogdbdatabase server's own status (PostgreSQL), connections to the catalog database, against the database server's connection limitNeeds: monitoring to collect it; no change to the application. Exists: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname = 'catalogdb', against SHOW max_connections.
9Basket store reachable and memory usedbasket store's own status (Redis), reachable and memory usedNeeds: monitoring to collect it; no change to the application. Exists: redis-cli PING.

The flow’s 5 alerts, each placed once: at the level it watches, and in the health layer of the measure it is built on (business, application or technology; a business alert is marked impact when it counts cases that failed what was expected of them, and health when it counts whether the work is happening).
